messages:
maria: heads-up: we're seeing a sudden surge in 5xx and 504s for hosted inference across eu-west-1 since the canary rolled ~20m ago. error rate ~6% -> 18% on production routes.

oncall-bot: ALERT: route-errors-high (eu-west-1) — 5xx spike detected. threshold breached: 12m ago. Paging: @sre-ops, @maria

sre-ops: investigating — pulling canary diff now. any recent config flags or rollout notes?

maria: merged canary for route-manager v2 at 2061232500. small traffic slice 5%. change toggles stickiness and a new header forwarding rule.

devon: seeing a lot of "upstream: request timeout (504)" and "gateway: missing auth header -> 500" in gateway logs. Dumping samples:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] req_id=0a1b2c path=/v1/generate status=500 err="auth: missing X-User-Token"
[2026-03-15T10:12:04Z] req_id=0a1b2d path=/v1/embeddings status=504 err="upstream timeout"
```

maria: that missing header lines up with the route-manager change that rewrites headers for canary nodes. maybe it dropped X-User-Token for some clients.

nishant: confirmed: canary env var ROUTE_FORWARD_MODE=strip_sensitive was accidentally enabled in the canary config. Should be "preserve".

kevin: oh no — that's why some auth calls fallback to anonymous -> 500s. Also saw auth service rate-limit alarms spike.

support-bot: customer-escalation: 3 enterprise customers report 5xx for hosted endpoints, case IDs #4521, #4522, #4523. Marked P1.

sre-ops: plan: 1) scale down canary to 0% traffic 2) roll back route-manager v2 flag 3) mitigate auth service rate limits. Can someone issue rollback?

maria: issuing rollback now. deploy-bot: `POST /deploy/rollback` in progress...

deploy-bot: Rollback started by maria for deploy route-manager-v2, change-set d193f. estimated 90s.

devon: while rollback happens, we should temp-route traffic to older gateway pool and enable header-preserve on edge. I can push edge ACL change.

sre-ops: please add a quick patch to auth-proxy to treat missing X-User-Token as 401 not 500, until we confirm all clients. reduces noisy 5xx and customer alerts.

nishant: small config patch ready: set ROUTE_FORWARD_MODE=preserve in canary config and auth proxy will log but not 5xx. ready to apply after rollback verification.

maria: rollback finished according to deploy-bot. verifying telemetry...
sre-ops: metrics trending down. 5xx dropped back to baseline ~1.3% over last 3m. 504s falling.

kevin: confirmed with support: customer #4522 sees success now. reaching out to others.
support-bot: update: #4521 resolved, #4522 resolved, #4523 awaiting customer confirmation (pinged).

maria: root cause: human error — canary config accidentally set ROUTE_FORWARD_MODE=strip_sensitive due to bad templating in helm values (values-canary.yml). variable default got inverted.

devon: repro steps for postmortem:
```
# reproduce locally
helm template charts/route-manager -f values-canary.yml | grep ROUTE_FORWARD_MODE
# show header drop
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer test" -H "X-User-Token: abc" https://canary-gw.local/v1/generate
```

nishant: short-term action items: 1) revert canary template to add a safety check 2) add CI lint to catch suspicious ROUTE_FORWARD_MODE values 3) make auth proxy return 401 for missing token 4) run targeted canary for 1% traffic with header-preserve enforced.

sre-ops: assigning: maria -> postmortem writeup, devon -> CI lint, nishant -> auth proxy change, kevin -> customer comms.

maria: filing incident ticket and postmortem. draft will include timeline, root cause, rollback commands, and customer impact.

kevin: note on billing: some customers saw failed requests but billing tallies only successful tokens; finance confirmed no double billing. I'll add a note in comms.

support-bot: action log: rollback completed; customers notified; monitoring alert cleared.

maria: quick follow-up: adding health-check into canary rollout: if any auth-related 5xx > 1% in the first 10m, auto-rollback.

devon: also gating ROUTE_FORWARD_MODE changes behind a feature flag that requires code-owner approval.

sre-ops: thanks everyone. keep an eye on related metrics for 24h. postmortem due EOD tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
